newsitem.title: USA: Financier Hoffenberg to get 20-year sentence.
newsitem.headline: Financier Hoffenberg to get 20-year sentence.

text.p: A federal judge plans to sentence financier Steven Hoffenberg, accused of running the largest Ponzi scheme in history, to 20 years in prison and to order him to pay more than $476 million in penalties.
U.S. District Judge Robert Sweet said in an opinion made public Wednesday that he plans to formally sentence Hoffenberg on Friday.

Hoffenberg had headed Towers Financial Corp., which filed for bankruptcy protection from creditors in 1993 after it was discovered that the flamboyant financier was using the company to operate what prosecutors called the largest Ponzi scheme in U.S. history.
Hoffenberg, who gained attention when he offered to rescue the New York Post in January 1993, pleaded guilty to conspiracy and fraud charges in April 1995.

He sold more than $450 million in fraudulent notes and bonds to investors and used some of the money collected from later investors to pay interest owed to the earlier ones. The rest of the money was used to run the Post and to operate his financial empire with inflated revenues and profits that made it appear to be a major health care financing company.
He recently asked to withdraw his guilty plea, claiming he was mentally unfit when he admitted to the fraud. Sweet denied the request.
